newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen shares plunge at close on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares plunge at close on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shenzhen shares plunged at Monday's close amid unexpected bearishness that has swept away buying interest since the return of Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty on July 1, brokers said.
The Shenzhen domestic A share index ended down 33.28 points or 8.08 percent to 378.35 points. The hard currency B share index lost 7.71 points or 5.7 percent to 127.69 points.
Turnover on the A market shrank to 4.8 billion yuan from Friday's 5.7 billion yuan whie turnover on the B share market rose to HK$50 million against HK$44 million on Friday.
"The market lost a major sentiment-support with the passing of the handover," an analyst at China Securities Co said.
Brokers said investor confidence had been hard hit after the media-hyped return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule on July 1 after 156 years as a British colony failed to generate strong buying.
"It is still a confidence problem," Song Bin, an analyst at Central-South Securities in Shenzhen, said. "When a market keeps falling, the flow of fresh money will certainly stop."
"The recent plunges could also be seen as a delayed reaction to the pull-out of state banks and listed firms and a faster market expansion pace," Song said.
China has ordered state banks and listed firms to stop share speculation, and has boosted the quota for new listings in an effort to soak up liquidity.
"Some investors are worrying that a long-term bear-run has started," Song added.
Brokers also attributed Monday's sharp falls to talk that securities authorities planned to increase supervision over listed firms' interim reports.
Any tightening would work to stop listed firms exaggerating their profits, an analyst at China Guotai Securities said. Listed firms must release their 1997 first-half reports by the end of August.
Brokers said they expected a rebound soon.
"Trading turnover has been contracting for the past few days, laying the ground work for a rebound," Song said.
None of the 48 Shenzhen-listed B shares gained.

China International Marine Containers (Group) was among the biggest B share losers, falling HK$0.85 to its 10-percent limit-down at HK$7.64. On the A share market, textile concern Shenzhen Victor Onward saw a 10 percent limit-down loss of 0.67 yuan to 5.99 yuan.
